Sam Seisen mentions that you must never cut through candles, and the only way one could still take this level under consideration, is if one cuts through candles on the left.

You'll see in the circles that level 3 has historic significance, and that it wasn't easily breached on revisit - price bounced up to S at 4. I've never understood what people mean by "cutting through candles". Here we simply have a decision made to break up through minor Supply after a rt to Demand - creating a good new Demand

2. Is the whole descend into your #1 revisit into the Demand level considered CP (17 OCT 21:00 till 18 OCT 02:20 in your chart)?

As the chart said, in that TF, price had CPed almost to point A - to the spike to the right and above.

3. What is a Swap Zone?

A swap zone is an area of price which had been used as Supply and Demand in the past

AdamH نوشت: 1. دربارهٔ #3، می‌گویی آن سطح «هنوز تست نشده بود»، اما می‌بینیم که کمی بعدتر به‌راحتی شکسته می‌شود. پس منظورت از «هنوز» چیست؟ Sam Seisen می‌گوید هرگز نباید از میان کندل‌ها رد شد، و تنها راهی که بشود این سطح را همچنان در نظر گرفت این است که آدم از میان کندل‌های سمت چپ رد شده باشد.

posts.t:
Simply look at it with a Supply/Demand view.

If all of the D's are spiked, and price breaks the low of the highest D, it will go to the next D. The whole cp zone can be viewed as a pole, the base of which is inside the lowest D of the cp.
